checks: All 24 migrations install into a fresh PostgreSQL test database
No customer or coach accounts seeded
All three v0.9.16 training articles seeded
RLS enabled; anonymous record reads denied
Migration 020 rerun preserves article records and coach edits
Migrations 021 and 022 upgrade an existing install: no expiry, no timezone (default Asia/Colombo), records and access unchanged; 022 re-runs safely
Client with no expiry date signs in and reads data as before (state ok, no days left)
Expiry, country and timezone set at creation are copied to the account; the last day is fully usable (days left 0)
Timezone boundary: open until 23:59:59 on the last day and closed from 00:00 the next day, in the client zone (Dubai 20:00 UTC, Colombo 18:30 UTC)
Expired client: RLS blocks records, events, saves and chat for an already-issued session; status reports expired
Two clients with the same date in different timezones expire at different moments (24 hours apart)
Daylight saving: America/New_York ends at 05:00 UTC in winter and 04:00 UTC in summer; local last day open, day after closed
No timezone set: the default timezone setting is used (and Asia/Colombo when none is set)
Invalid timezones (not IANA) and countries are rejected for client profiles, the default setting and accounts
Renewing or removing the expiry date restores access without a new login
Paused and archived clients are blocked and reported as paused / archived (status takes precedence over expiry)
RLS: a client reads only its own account row, cannot change its expiry date, country or timezone; anonymous callers cannot query access status
Invalid expiry dates are rejected; access status includes the coach support contact
Migration 023 aborts before patching when an earlier patch (014) is missing, and leaves the database unchanged
Migration 023 keeps the 009, 010 and 014 patches, applies patches A–D and the readable() patch exactly once, and re-runs without changes
Client saves a draft while onboarding; only that client and the coach can read it; no package feature needed (training-only package); clients cannot write another client's intake or set reopened
Submitting needs every answer, confirmation and the consent tick; the server stamps the time and profile snapshot; the client then cannot write, through panda_save or directly

Coach sets an intake to reopened and the client can edit (it stays reopened while they save drafts) and resubmit, after which it locks again; an active client can only start an intake the coach has opened
Intake answers never reach panda_events: batches containing client_intake get the fixed label, even with a custom label or a clients change in the same batch, as client and as coach
A clients + client_intake batch saves atomically: both records commit together (snapshot includes the new profile), and a failure in either record rolls back both

Lift validation: unknown rejects a weight, reps or estimate; a submitted working set needs 1–20 whole reps; 1RM rejects reps; kg/lb limits; the strict shape rejects unknown or missing keys and invalid focus muscles

health_flag is set by the server from chest pain, heart disease, stroke, coronary disease, light-headedness, pregnancy or a contraindication; values sent for it, submitted_at or submitted_profile are ignored
Neither the client nor the coach can delete an intake through panda_save
Migration 010 still applies after 023: a nutrition-only client records water, but not steps
Intake retention is settings/brand.intake_retention_months (seeded 24): 1–120 whole months or empty for none; invalid values are rejected
Re-running migration 023 on a database with intakes leaves every client record and the coach's retention setting unchanged
Migration 024 aborts when migration 023 is missing, and leaves the database unchanged
Migration 024 leaves panda_save and readable() unchanged, stamps clients archived before the upgrade once (no revision bump), and re-runs without changes
Archiving a client records archived_at; later saves of the archived client keep the original date, even when the row sent omits it
Un-archiving (to active, paused or onboarding) removes archived_at; archiving again records a new date
The coach cannot set, change or clear archived_at: a value sent on an active client is dropped, on an archived client it is replaced by the server date
A client cannot send archived_at or archive themselves, cannot update the row directly, and still saves their own profile; direct database writes cannot set it either
Latest source initializes without JS runtime errors and without a backend connection
Expiry rules in the browser: 7/3/1-day tiers, wording, zone labels, and end instants identical to Postgres in every tested zone (DST included)
Expired login shows the expired message with the coach support contact and leaves no session behind
Paused login shows the paused message
Archived login shows the archived message
Without the status lookup (older database), inactive and expired accounts still get a clear message
Wrong password still shows the normal credentials error, without an access notice
Banner: none at 8 days; shown at 7, 3, 2, 1 days and on the last day with the exact end (Dubai time) and contacts; dismissed for the session, back at the next sign-in
Banner days come from the timezone sent by the server: the same date is 1 day away in Honolulu and the last day in Kiritimati
A client already signed in is signed out with the expired message once the server reports expiry
Client with no expiry date signs in to the dashboard with no warning banner
Coach Access dialog shows days left and the exact end in the client’s timezone
Coach form: country first (default Sri Lanka), zones by city for multi-zone countries, manual override, end sentence, quick lengths and renewal; list colours and next steps per client timezone
Coach portal loads client_intake records into state (assemble) with the server-set fields
Restoring a backup without client_intake keeps every intake (no deletion sent, database unchanged) and still applies the backup's other changes
A backup with an empty client_intake list is refused as a whole (intakes cannot be deleted) and changes nothing
Commit sends clients before client_intake in one batch (flatten emits the intake)
validate() accepts a missing or valid client_intake list and rejects other shapes or more than 20,000 rows; PandaRecipes.migrate defaults it to []
limits: Hosted Auth, Edge Function and two-client browser acceptance require customer accounts
Local DOM checks are not visual desktop/mobile testing
